title: Family & people
goal: Talk about your family, say who is related to whom, and describe people with 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her'.
intro:
Family vocabulary in Kannada is much more precise than in English: there is no single word for 'brother' or 'sister', only *elder* brother (ಅಣ್ಣ) and *younger* brother (ತಮ್ಮ), elder sister (ಅಕ್ಕ) and younger sister (ತಂಗಿ). These words are also used as friendly titles for strangers: a rickshaw driver might be ಅಣ್ಣ, a shopkeeper's wife ಅಕ್ಕ.

Grammatically, this unit introduces the **possessive** ('of') ending and the way Kannada forms **plurals**.

There are four of us at home.

grammar.title: Possessives: 'my', 'your', and the ending -ಅ ('of')
grammar.body:
Possessive pronouns: ನನ್ನ *nanna* my, ನಿನ್ನ *ninna* your (inf.), ನಿಮ್ಮ *nimma* your (pol./pl.), ಅವನ *avana* his, ಅವಳ *avaḷa* her, ಅದರ *adara* its, ನಮ್ಮ *namma* our, ಅವರ *avara* their / his/her (resp.).

For nouns, the possessive (genitive) ending is **-ಅ**, joined with a linking sound:
• after -ಇ/-ಎ: add ಯ → ರವಿಯ *raviya* 'Ravi's', ಅಜ್ಜಿಯ 'grandma's', ಮನೆಯ 'of the house'
• people/kin ending in -ಅ: add ನ → ಅಮ್ಮನ *ammana* 'mum's', ಅಣ್ಣನ 'elder brother's', ಹುಡುಗನ 'the boy's'
• things ending in -ಅ: add ದ → ಮರದ *marada* 'of the tree'
• words ending in -ಉ: add ಇನ → ಊರಿನ *ūrina* 'of the town'

The possessor always comes first: 'Ravi's mother's house' = ರವಿಯ ಅಮ್ಮನ ಮನೆ.

examples.en: The people of my town are good.

grammar.title: Gender, plurals and 'I have'
grammar.body:
Kannada nouns have **natural gender**: men are masculine, women feminine, and everything else (animals, things, ideas, babies) is neuter. Gender matters for verb agreement (ಅವನು ಇದ್ದಾನೆ / ಅವಳು ಇದ್ದಾಳೆ / ಅದು ಇದೆ), not for adjectives.

**Plurals:**
• Most nouns add **-ಗಳು** *-gaḷu*: ಮನೆ → ಮನೆಗಳು, ಪುಸ್ತಕ → ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳು
• Human nouns usually add **-ಅರು** *-aru*: ಹುಡುಗ → ಹುಡುಗರು, ಹುಡುಗಿ → ಹುಡುಗಿಯರು, ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ → ಸ್ನೇಹಿತರು
• Kinship terms add **-ಅಂದಿರು**: ಅಣ್ಣ → ಅಣ್ಣಂದಿರು, ಅಕ್ಕ → ಅಕ್ಕಂದಿರು
• Irregular: ಮಗು → ಮಕ್ಕಳು

**'I have'** (family, things, time) uses the **dative** -ಗೆ + ಇರು: ನನಗೆ ಒಬ್ಬ ತಮ್ಮ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ 'to me a younger brother is' = 'I have a younger brother'. The verb agrees with the thing possessed. Counting people uses special forms: ಒಬ್ಬ (m) / ಒಬ್ಬಳು (f) 'one', ಇಬ್ಬರು 'two', ಮೂವರು 'three', ನಾಲ್ವರು 'four', or simply number + ಜನ 'people'.

examples.en: There are lots of houses in our town.
Do you have an elder brother?
examples.note: Someone else's elder relatives take the respectful plural verb (about your own elder brother, ಇದ್ದಾನೆ is common).

dialogue.title: The family photo
dialogue.setting: Priya shows her colleague Tom a photo from her cousin's wedding on her phone.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ಇವರು ನನ್ನ ಅಜ್ಜಿ. ಅವರ ಪಕ್ಕ ನನ್ನ ಅಪ್ಪ ಅಮ್ಮ.
lines.roman: ivaru nanna ajji. avara pakka nanna appa amma.
lines.en: This is my grandmother. Next to her are my dad and mum.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Is this boy your younger brother?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ಹೌದು, ಅವನು ನನ್ನ ತಮ್ಮ. ಅವನು ಇನ್ನೂ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ.
lines.roman: haudu, avanu nanna tamma. avanu innū vidyārthi.
lines.en: Yes, he's my younger brother. He's still a student.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Do you have an elder sister?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ಇಲ್ಲ, ಒಬ್ಬ ಅಣ್ಣ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ. ಅವನು ಅಮೆರಿಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ.
lines.roman: illa, obba aṇṇa iddāne. avanu amerikadalli iddāne.
lines.en: No, I have an elder brother. He lives in America.

culture: Kinship words are used constantly with non-relatives: ಅಣ್ಣ for a man a bit older than you, ಅಕ್ಕ for a woman, ಅಂಕಲ್/ಆಂಟಿ (from English) for people of your parents' age, and ಅಜ್ಜ/ಅಜ್ಜಿ for the elderly. Siblings are usually called by kin term, not by name: a younger sibling calls an elder brother ಅಣ್ಣ, never just 'Ravi'. Traditionally, in many Kannada communities, marriage between a girl and her ಮಾವ (mother's brother) or a cross-cousin was common, which is why ಮಾವ means both 'mother's brother' and 'father-in-law'.

tip.title: Whose? ನನ್ನ, ನಿಮ್ಮ and -ಅ 'of'
tip.body:
- **ನನ್ನ** my · **ನಿಮ್ಮ** your · **ನಮ್ಮ** our (often used for 'my' family) · **ಅವನ / ಅವಳ / ಅವರ** his / her / their.
- For a noun add **-ಅ**: with ನ after people ending in -ಅ (ಅಮ್ಮ**ನ** ಹೆಸರು 'mum's name'), with ಯ after -ಇ/-ಎ (ಅಜ್ಜಿ**ಯ** ಮನೆ).
- The owner always comes first: ನನ್ನ ಅಪ್ಪನ ಹೆಸರು 'my dad's name'.

lessons.title: Brothers and sisters

tip.title: I have: 'to me … is'
tip.body:
- 'I have a brother' is 'to me a brother is': **ನನಗೆ** ಒಬ್ಬ ತಮ್ಮ **ಇದ್ದಾನೆ**.
- The verb agrees with what you have: ತಮ್ಮ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ, ತಂಗಿ ಇದ್ದಾಳೆ, elders (with respect) ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. Don't have one: **ಇಲ್ಲ**.
- Counting people: **ಒಬ್ಬ** (m) / **ಒಬ್ಬಳು** (f) 'one', **ಇಬ್ಬರು** 'two'.

new: ನನಗೆ ಒಬ್ಬ ಅಣ್ಣ, ಒಬ್ಬಳು ತಂಗಿ ಇದ್ದಾರೆ

sentences.en: Do you have a younger sister?
No, I don't have a younger sister.
My elder sister lives in Bengaluru.

lessons.title: Talking about your children
new: ಇಬ್ಬರು ಮಕ್ಕಳು, ಒಬ್ಬ ಮಗ, ಒಬ್ಬಳು ಮಗಳು

tip.title: Married? "Has the wedding happened?"
tip.body:
- 'Are you married?' is 'to you, has the wedding happened?': ನಿಮಗೆ ಮದುವೆ **ಆಗಿದೆಯಾ**?
- Yes: ಮದುವೆ **ಆಗಿದೆ**. Not yet: ಇನ್ನೂ **ಆಗಿಲ್ಲ**.
- The person takes **-ಗೆ**, as with 'I have': ನನಗೆ, ಅವಳಿಗೆ, ತಮ್ಮನಿಗೆ, ಅಜ್ಜನಿಗೆ.

sentences.en: Grandpa and grandma live in our hometown.

lessons.title: Uncles, aunts and a full house

sentences.en: My uncle (dad's younger brother) lives in Mysuru.
My uncle's son lives in London.
How many people live in your town?
There are lots of people in our house.
There are a lot of people here.
He isn't my older uncle, he's my younger uncle.

tip.title: One and many
tip.body:
- People add **-ರು**: ಹುಡುಗ → ಹುಡುಗ**ರು**, ಹುಡುಗಿ → ಹುಡುಗಿ**ಯರು**, ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ → ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ**ರು**, ಗಂಡಸು → ಗಂಡಸರು.
- Things add **-ಗಳು**: ಮನೆ → ಮನೆಗಳು. The odd one out: ಮಗು → **ಮಕ್ಕಳು**.
- A friend who is a woman is **ಸ್ನೇಹಿತೆ**.
